pitch: Treasury rules in plain English, executed as deterministic onchain flows on Arc. AI compiles one sentence into one of three fixed templates (Split, Sweep, Bridge), then leaves the loop.

hackathon.name: Encode x Arc Programmable Money Hackathon

2026-08-06: interpreter live. Caught a real compile defect (model filled readback prose but left savingsAddress empty, ~1 in 3) - validator failed closed and turned it into a refusal; fixed via sharper field descriptions + effort high. Only 3 files touch the model, entire runtime path greps clean.

2026-08-07: SweepRule wired end to end and deployed. Interpreter now knows three templates; battery 13/13 with two new refusal cases (scheduled same-chain sweep, partial sweep) and template-identity assertions so a sweep compiled as a bridge fails the test

2026-08-07: keeper defect found and fixed. HTTP poller swallowed every error and, on failure, re-read only the last 5 blocks forever; on Arc at ~5 blocks/sec that is a permanent blind spot. It silently missed a real payment during testing. Now scans a committed block cursor in chunks and surfaces errors. Re-tested: keeper caught a live payment and settled both a native and an ERC-20 deposit in one execute
2026-08-07: keeper writes to data/executions.json, so the UI execution log shows real activity instead of only deployments; entries carry a trigger (deploy/payment/schedule/manual)

2026-08-07: BridgeRule gets a scheduled ticker. Payment-reactive rules have a log to react to; an interval rule has none. The tick simulates first, so an early tick costs no gas and the contract still enforces the schedule

2026-08-07: two superseded BridgeRule versions (0x650cc26b, 0x83a9e5a6) were still in the store with an incompatible ruleState() shape, decoding to nonsense and about to be poked by the new ticker. Added a retired flag; keeper and API skip them
